missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Дворец' is the nominative subject, keeping its fleeting vowel 'е'. 'Этот' and 'старый' are the agreeing masculine forms. A clean descriptive model.
Strategic focus: Accusative direct object. 'Дворец' is the accusative object; as an inanimate masculine noun it keeps the nominative shape. 'Красивый' agrees in the masculine accusative.
Strategic focus: Genitive after a preposition. 'Дворца' is the genitive after 'возле'; the fleeting vowel 'е' drops in every case but the nominative singular. A core declension point.
Strategic focus: Dative with 'к'. 'Дворцу' is the dative after 'к', and the fleeting vowel again drops. 'Старому' is the agreeing masculine dative adjective. Marks approach toward a goal.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'Во дворце' uses the prepositional 'дворце' after 'в' to mark location. 'Большом' is the agreeing masculine prepositional adjective.
Strategic focus: Instrumental case. 'Дворцом' is the instrumental governed by 'восхищаться'. 'Этим' agrees in the masculine instrumental. The fleeting vowel stays dropped here too.

missions.phrase: Мы идём во дворец на экскурсию.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Accusative of direction. 'Во дворец' uses the accusative after 'в' to express motion toward the building; 'во' appears before the consonant cluster. A go-somewhere pattern.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural. 'Дворцов' is the genitive plural required after 'много'. The plural stem keeps the dropped vowel and takes the ending '-ов'. Useful for quantity.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural subject. 'Дворцы' is the nominative plural, the subject of 'привлекают'. 'Старинные' is the agreeing plural adjective. Note the consonant before '-ы'.
Strategic focus: Genitive of source. 'Из дворца' uses the genitive after 'из' to express motion out of the place; the fleeting vowel drops. The natural counterpart to 'во дворец'.
